explainers.ar:
Where This Comes From

Accounts Receivable

Customer Ledger Balance, and its age.

The cards give the total and the invoices behind it; the panels show who owes the most, how long it has been, and why the invoices say otherwise.
How It Is Put Together
Where It Is Kept
General Ledger, by Customer
How It Is Worked Out
Each Customer Ledger Balance: debits less credits. Customers in credit are counted separately.
Why Not Invoice Outstanding
Where a payment is never matched to the invoice it pays, the invoice still shows as unpaid though the money is in. The open invoices' own total is shown beside the Customer Ledger's, with the reason for the difference.
How the Ages Are Set
Unreconciled payments and credits are set against the customer's oldest invoices and opening balances first; what is left is aged from its Due Date to the latest date the records cover
Unpaid Sales Invoices
Count of unpaid Sales Invoices, and their Outstanding Amount
Checked Against
The business's ERPNext, line by line, under Settings, Businesses, Check Figures
explainers.ledger:
Where This Comes From

Party Ledger Balance vs Invoice Outstanding

Each Customer and Supplier Ledger Balance, beside Invoice Outstanding.

Each name opens its General Ledger.
How It Is Put Together
Invoice Outstanding
Outstanding Amount on the open invoices
Party Ledger Balance
General Ledger balance: a customer's debits less credits, a supplier's credits less debits. Negative means in credit.
Difference and Why
Unreconciled payments; allocations on invoices whose Outstanding Amount was not updated; Journal Entries and Credit Notes with no invoice reference; less amounts on no invoice, such as opening balances. Any remainder is shown as unexplained.
The Ages
After unreconciled payments and credits are set against the oldest open items
Putting It Right
Reconcile them in Accounts, Payment Reconciliation. Outstanding Amounts then agree with the Ledger Balance.

explainers.cover:
Where This Comes From

Promised Orders — Cover

Every Sales Order line To Deliver, with the stock or purchase that covers it.

Each row opens the order line, its stock and its purchase chain, with links to the documents in ERPNext.
How It Is Put Together
Where It Is Kept
ERPNext: the open sales orders, the stock in each warehouse, and the purchase orders, material requests, Purchase Receipts and Purchase Invoices
What Counts
Submitted Sales Orders not Completed or Closed, line by line, with Qty To Deliver
Linked
A purchase order or material request raised from the sales order (Create, Purchase Order or Material Request) names the order it is for, and is followed to the Purchase Receipt and the Purchase Invoice
Likely
Where nothing names the order: an open purchase order for the same item, raised shortly before or after the order and linked to no other order. Each is counted once, oldest promise first, with the reason given
Stock
What the line's own warehouse holds, then any other warehouse goods are sold from, shared out oldest promise first so that no unit is counted twice
The States
In Stock, Received, On Order, Requested, Partly Covered, Not Ordered, Not a Stock Item. Late to Customer when the delivery date has passed; Supplier Late when the purchase order is past the date asked for
The Settings
How far before and after an order a purchase order may be raised and still count as likely: Settings, Recommendations, Promised to customers, not ordered
